name: Eliada
overview: Eliada was a male commander from the tribe of Benjamin who served under King Jehoshaphat. He is noted for leading a substantial force of 200,000 men, demonstrating a significant military role within the kingdom of Judah. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliada means 'G-d knows,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's knowledge and sovereignty. This proper name is recorded in 2 Chronicles 17:17 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Eliada is explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Eliada's importance in the biblical narrative lies in his leadership role as a military commander during the reign of Jehoshaphat. Commanding 200,000 men signifies his trusted position and the strength of Judah's armed forces under God's providence. His mention highlights the organized and divinely guided governance of Jehoshaphat's kingdom.
